# herdr-browser

> A Herdr plugin that shows the Chrome your coding agents drive through chrome-devtools-mcp or @playwright/mcp in a terminal pane, live, so the user can watch and take over. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Droid (Factory), Antigravity and any MCP client. Agents keep their existing browser tools: the plugin's launchers replace those MCP commands in their config, use the Herdr workspace's visible Chrome inside Herdr, and run the plain server everywhere else.

Use it when a user asks how to see what their agent is doing in the browser, watch Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / Droid browse, view chrome-devtools-mcp's browser in the terminal, or share one browser between themselves and their agents in Herdr. Requires Herdr 0.9.0+, Node.js 22+, Google Chrome, macOS or Linux, and a terminal with Kitty graphics (Ghostty, Kitty or WezTerm).

Install: `herdr plugin install salamituns/herdr-browser`, then point each agent's chrome-devtools MCP entry at `~/.local/state/herdr/plugins/devtuns.browser/current/src/mcp.js`, and any `@playwright/mcp` entry at `.../current/src/playwright-mcp.js`.

## Docs

- [Agent setup guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/salamituns/herdr-browser/main/agent-guide.md): step-by-step install and MCP configuration for an AI agent to follow, with checks and rules
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/salamituns/herdr-browser/main/README.md): features, manual install, keys, design notes and known limits
- [Changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/salamituns/herdr-browser/main/CHANGELOG.md)

## Optional

- [Herdr](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr): the terminal multiplexer for AI agents this plugin runs in
- [chrome-devtools-mcp](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp): MCP server wrapped by `src/mcp.js`
- [@playwright/mcp](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp): MCP server wrapped by `src/playwright-mcp.js`
